milestones.label: Pathwise KPZ solution
milestones.work: M. Hairer, Solving the KPZ equation, arXiv:1109.6811 (2011)
milestones.description: A pathwise solution theory for KPZ precedes the general regularity-structure framework.

milestones.label: Regularity structures introduced
milestones.work: M. Hairer, A theory of regularity structures, arXiv:1303.5113 (2013)
milestones.description: The preprint defines models and a calculus for singular stochastic PDEs.
milestones.note: The same paper states and applies the framework.

milestones.label: Phi-four three dynamics constructed
milestones.work: M. Hairer, A theory of regularity structures, arXiv:1303.5113 (2013)
milestones.description: The paper uses regularity structures to construct the stochastic quantization process for the three-dimensional Phi-four model.

evidence.claim: The abstract explicitly names the Phi-four-three application

milestones.note: The same work truly plays both first-statement and first-application roles.

milestones.label: Rough-path course incorporates regularity structures
milestones.work: P. K. Friz and M. Hairer, A Course on Rough Paths, second edition, Springer (2020)
milestones.description: A systematic second-edition text includes an introduction to regularity structures.

works.whyItMatters: Defines the framework and constructs its first major SPDE application

notes: The 2011 KPZ work is a precursor, not a 2011 publication of the general regularity-structures theory. The Inventiones 2014 journal date follows the public 2013 preprint.

milestones.label: Perfectoid spaces and tilting introduced
milestones.work: P. Scholze, Perfectoid spaces, arXiv:1111.4914 (2011)
milestones.description: The preprint defines perfectoid rings and spaces and their characteristic-changing tilting operation.
milestones.note: The same work defines and applies the theory.

milestones.label: Tilting applied to weight-monodromy cases
milestones.work: P. Scholze, Perfectoid spaces, arXiv:1111.4914 (2011)
milestones.description: The paper deduces cases of the weight-monodromy conjecture by reduction to equal characteristic.

evidence.claim: The abstract states the target application

milestones.note: The same work truly plays both first-statement and first-application roles.

milestones.label: Perfectoid spaces used in rigid-analytic p-adic Hodge theory
milestones.work: P. Scholze, p-adic Hodge theory for rigid-analytic varieties, arXiv:1205.3463 (2012)
milestones.description: A comparison theorem for rigid-analytic varieties explicitly relies on perfectoid spaces.

milestones.label: Perfectoid-space survey
milestones.work: P. Scholze, Perfectoid Spaces: A survey, arXiv:1303.5948 (2013)
milestones.description: The survey organizes the new theory, applications and open problems.

works.whyItMatters: Introduces tilting and applies it to weight-monodromy

notes: The public arXiv posting is 2011, preceding the 2012 journal issue. The catalogue's 2020 institutional date has no checked field-naming institution and is not promoted.

canonicalName: MIP*=RE: entangled provers, computability and the Connes embedding problem

milestones.label: Entangled-prover NEXP lower bound
milestones.work: T. Ito and T. Vidick, A multi-prover interactive proof for NEXP sound against entangled provers, arXiv:1207.0550 (2012)
milestones.description: A lower bound for MIP* predates the equality with recursively enumerable languages.

milestones.label: NEEXP lower bound for MIP*
milestones.work: A. Natarajan and J. Wright, NEEXP in MIP*, arXiv:1904.05870 (2019)
milestones.description: The stronger lower bound is part of the proof trajectory toward MIP*=RE.

milestones.label: MIP*=RE theorem posted
milestones.work: Z. Ji, A. Natarajan, T. Vidick, J. Wright and H. Yuen, MIP*=RE, arXiv:2001.04383 (2020)
milestones.description: The preprint states the equality of entangled multiprover proofs and recursively enumerable languages.
milestones.note: The same paper proves the theorem and its consequences.

milestones.label: Halting problem reduced to nonlocal-game value
milestones.work: Z. Ji et al., MIP*=RE, arXiv:2001.04383 (2020)
milestones.description: The theorem yields undecidability of entangled game value and a negative answer to Connes embedding.

evidence.claim: The abstract explicitly states both consequences

milestones.note: The same work truly plays both first-statement and first-application roles.

works.whyItMatters: Co-proves the theorem linking quantum games and computability

notes: The inherited conceptual range 2011–13 describes antecedents, not the 2020 theorem. These precursors are separate milestones. This event overlaps Q46's quantum-game history but has a different target theorem.

canonicalName: Arc spaces of singularities and partition identities

milestones.label: Arc-space/partition correspondence posted
milestones.work: C. Bruschek, H. Mourtada and J. Schepers, Arc Spaces and Rogers-Ramanujan Identities, arXiv:1101.4950 (2011)
milestones.description: The paper links Hilbert-Poincare series of arc spaces to partition generating functions.
milestones.note: The same work states and applies the connection.

milestones.label: Double-point arc space yields Rogers-Ramanujan identity
milestones.work: C. Bruschek, H. Mourtada and J. Schepers, Arc Spaces and Rogers-Ramanujan Identities, DMTCS Proceedings AO (2011)
milestones.description: The 2011 proceeding applies the arc-space series of a double point to integer partitions without equal or consecutive parts.

evidence.claim: Published 2011 proceeding and abstract identify the double-point application

milestones.note: This is a published version of the founding preprint and documents the same first application.

milestones.label: Differential-ideal Groebner bases extend the partition connection
milestones.work: P. Afsharijoo and H. Mourtada, Partition identities and application to infinite dimensional Groebner basis and viceversa, arXiv:2006.09147 (2020)
milestones.description: A later paper relates differential-ideal Groebner bases to Rogers-Ramanujan-type partition identities.

works.whyItMatters: Co-links arc spaces of singularities and partition identities

notes: The inherited Craig–van Ittersum–Ono 2024 citation concerns partitions detecting primes, not this arc-space construction; it is not included as a development. The 2011 preprint and proceeding are the same project, not independent priority claims.

canonicalName: Virtual fundamental cycles via homotopical algebra

milestones.label: Intrinsic normal cone and virtual class
milestones.work: K. Behrend and B. Fantechi, The intrinsic normal cone, arXiv:alg-geom/9601010 (1996)
milestones.description: An earlier algebraic construction of virtual classes provides a distinct foundation.

milestones.label: Pardon introduces implicit-atlas VFC package
milestones.work: J. Pardon, An algebraic approach to virtual fundamental cycles on moduli spaces of pseudo-holomorphic curves, arXiv:1309.2370 (2013)
milestones.description: The preprint presents an algebraic, sheaf-theoretic virtual-cycle construction using implicit atlases.
milestones.note: The same paper states and applies this particular construction.

milestones.label: Implicit-atlas package applied to symplectic invariants
milestones.work: J. Pardon, An algebraic approach to virtual fundamental cycles on moduli spaces of pseudo-holomorphic curves, arXiv:1309.2370 (2013)
milestones.description: The paper gives definitions of Gromov–Witten invariants and Hamiltonian Floer homology and an S1-localization calculation.

evidence.claim: The abstract explicitly names these applications

milestones.note: The same work truly plays both first-statement and first-application roles.

works.citation: An algebraic approach to virtual fundamental cycles on moduli spaces of pseudo-holomorphic curves

notes: The inherited 2012 date is earlier than the checked 2013 public preprint and is not used. The event name's 'homotopical algebra' is broader than the paper's own description, which emphasizes algebraic/sheaf-theoretic implicit atlases.

milestones.label: Controlled rough paths
milestones.work: M. Gubinelli, Controlling Rough Paths, arXiv:math/0306433 (2003)
milestones.description: Controlled rough paths supply one of the ingredients later adapted to singular PDEs.

milestones.label: Paracontrolled distributions introduced
milestones.work: M. Gubinelli, P. Imkeller and N. Perkowski, Paracontrolled distributions and singular PDEs, arXiv:1210.2684 (2012)
milestones.description: The paper combines paradifferential calculus with controlled rough paths for singular PDEs.
milestones.note: The same paper introduces and applies the approach.

milestones.label: Paracontrolled method applied to model SPDEs
milestones.work: M. Gubinelli, P. Imkeller and N. Perkowski, Paracontrolled distributions and singular PDEs, arXiv:1210.2684 (2012)
milestones.description: The authors treat fractional-Brownian, Burgers-type and parabolic-Anderson model problems.

evidence.claim: The abstract explicitly lists the model problems

milestones.note: The same work truly plays both first-statement and first-application roles.

notes: The Forum of Mathematics, Pi publication is 2015; the same work was publicly available in 2012.

milestones.label: Classical Ramanujan graph constructions
milestones.work: A. Lubotzky, R. Phillips and P. Sarnak, Ramanujan graphs, Combinatorica 8 (1988)
milestones.description: Explicit constructions cover special degrees before the all-degree interlacing result.

evidence.claim: Publisher record dates the classical paper to 1988

milestones.label: Interlacing families for all-degree Ramanujan graphs
milestones.work: A. Marcus, D. A. Spielman and N. Srivastava, Interlacing Families I: Bipartite Ramanujan Graphs of All Degrees, arXiv:1304.4132 (2013)
milestones.description: The public preprint introduces interlacing-polynomial existence arguments and states all-degree bipartite Ramanujan graph families.
milestones.note: The same paper introduces and applies this interlacing method.

milestones.label: Interlacing applied to graph 2-lifts
milestones.work: A. Marcus, D. A. Spielman and N. Srivastava, Interlacing Families I: Bipartite Ramanujan Graphs of All Degrees, arXiv:1304.4132 (2013)
milestones.description: The method proves existence of good 2-lifts and infinite bipartite Ramanujan families in every degree above two.
milestones.note: The same work truly plays both first-statement and first-application roles.

works.citation: Interlacing Families I: Bipartite Ramanujan Graphs of All Degrees
works.whyItMatters: Co-develops interlacing families for all-degree expanders

notes: This catalogue event bundles the 1988 graph notion and 2013 interlacing method. The 1988 paper is retained as a phase precursor, so derived dates describe the new transfer rather than the birth of Ramanujan graphs.

milestones.label: Kadison–Singer problem posed
milestones.work: R. V. Kadison and I. M. Singer, Extensions of Pure States, American Journal of Mathematics 81 (1959)
milestones.description: The original operator-algebra problem predates its interlacing-polynomial solution.

evidence.claim: Publisher record dates the original article to 1959

milestones.label: Interlacing families I establishes method
milestones.work: A. Marcus, D. A. Spielman and N. Srivastava, Interlacing Families I, arXiv:1304.4132 (2013)
milestones.description: An April preprint develops the interlacing method for Ramanujan graphs before the Kadison–Singer transfer.

milestones.label: Kadison–Singer solution posted
milestones.work: A. Marcus, D. A. Spielman and N. Srivastava, Interlacing Families II: Mixed Characteristic Polynomials and the Kadison-Singer Problem, arXiv:1306.3969 (2013)
milestones.description: The public preprint states a positive solution through interlacing and mixed characteristic polynomials.
milestones.note: The same paper states and applies the method.

milestones.label: Mixed characteristic polynomials prove paving bounds
milestones.work: A. Marcus, D. A. Spielman and N. Srivastava, Interlacing Families II: Mixed Characteristic Polynomials and the Kadison-Singer Problem, arXiv:1306.3969 (2013)
milestones.description: The method proves Weaver's KS2 and explicit paving consequences implying Kadison–Singer.

evidence.claim: The abstract identifies these target conjectures

milestones.note: The same work truly plays both first-statement and first-application roles.

works.citation: Interlacing Families II: Mixed Characteristic Polynomials and the Kadison-Singer Problem

notes: The original 1959 question and the 2013 interlacing proof are different stages. The 2015 Annals publication follows the public June 2013 preprint.

canonicalName: Liouville quantum gravity, the Brownian map and SLE

milestones.label: Schramm's LERW/UST scaling-limit work posted
milestones.work: O. Schramm, Scaling limits of loop-erased random walks and uniform spanning trees, arXiv:math/9904022 (1999)
milestones.description: SLE-related scaling-limit methods precede the later random-surface metric construction.

milestones.label: QLE metric on Liouville quantum gravity proposed
milestones.work: J. Miller and S. Sheffield, Liouville quantum gravity and the Brownian map I: The QLE(8/3,0) metric, arXiv:1507.00719 (2015)
milestones.description: The first series paper constructs a metric on a dense subset of the Liouville quantum gravity sphere.

milestones.label: LQG metric identified with the Brownian map
milestones.work: J. Miller and S. Sheffield, Liouville quantum gravity and the Brownian map II: geodesics and continuity of the embedding, arXiv:1605.03563 (2016)
milestones.description: The QLE metric is extended continuously to the sphere and its metric-measure law is identified with the Brownian map.

evidence.claim: First public preprint posted May 2016; abstract states the identification

works.citation: Liouville quantum gravity and the Brownian map II: geodesics and continuity of the embedding

notes: The 2015 part I paper does not yet establish the full law equivalence; part II does so in 2016. This record concerns that specific metric bridge, not the first definition of LQG or SLE.

canonicalName: Kakeya and Bourgain-Guth, decoupling for Vinogradov

milestones.label: Bourgain–Guth multilinear restriction argument
milestones.work: J. Bourgain and L. Guth, Bounds on oscillatory integral operators based on multilinear estimates, arXiv:1012.3760 (2010)
milestones.description: Multilinear estimates improve restriction bounds and connect to curved Kakeya problems.

milestones.label: Sharp l2 decoupling proved
milestones.work: J. Bourgain and C. Demeter, The proof of the l2 Decoupling Conjecture, arXiv:1403.5335 (2014)
milestones.description: The public paper proves the decoupling conjecture for positive-curvature hypersurfaces and cones.

milestones.label: Decoupling proves Vinogradov mean-value conjecture
milestones.work: J. Bourgain, C. Demeter and L. Guth, Proof of the main conjecture in Vinogradov's mean value theorem for degrees higher than three, arXiv:1512.01565 (2015)
milestones.description: A sharp decoupling inequality for curves yields the main conjecture in Vinogradov's mean-value theorem for degrees above three.

evidence.claim: First public preprint posted December 2015; abstract identifies the method

milestones.label: Decoupling study guide
milestones.work: J. Bourgain and C. Demeter, A study guide for the l2 Decoupling Theorem, arXiv:1604.06032 (2016)
milestones.description: A self-contained proof organizes the decoupling theorem for readers.

works.citation: The proof of the l2 Decoupling Conjecture
works.whyItMatters: Co-proves sharp decoupling, later applied to Vinogradov

notes: The event bundles the 2010 Bourgain–Guth restriction method, 2014 Bourgain–Demeter decoupling, and 2015 Vinogradov application. The 2016 Annals date is later than the public 2015 preprint.
